From: Helix Health Procurement <procurement@helix-health.com>

Cc: Helix CloudOps <cloudops@helix-health.com>, Helix Health Legal <legal@helix-health.com>

Subject: Request: Custom SLA addendum and order form language for Helix Health

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement, our legal and cloudops teams asked us to document availability and latency commitments in an SLA addendum (to attach to the MSA/SOW) and to annotate the order form language so it maps to our procurement system. High-level asks: 

- Target availability: 99.95% monthly (with defined measurement windows and credit schedule).
- Latency: P95 inference latency <= 250ms for text-generation endpoints under expected traffic (see profile below).
- Data residency: EU-only storage for model logs and KV caches (Helix will provide VPC guidance).
- Evidence: SOC2 report, uptime reports, and a short ops runbook showing incident escalation and regional failover behavior.

Attached is our redlined MSA (Helix_MSA_Redline.pdf) and a short traffic profile snapshot. Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to the availability/latency targets for a Dedicated capacity or Private deployment? If there are carve-outs (e.g., scheduled maintenance, force majeure, third-party outages), please highlight them in the addendum.

Finally, our procurement team would like a 30-day pilot clause (limited volume) that includes a performance verification window before committing to a 12-month reserved capacity order.

Can we sync today or early next week to align on language and next steps?

Thanks,
Laura Jenkins
Head of Procurement — Helix Health
procurement@helix-health.com

Attachments: Helix_MSA_Redline.pdf, helix_traffic_profile.csv

Hi Laura — great to hear and thanks for the redline.

Short answer: we can support a custom SLA addendum and annotated order form. Options we typically surface for availability/latency guarantees are: Dedicated capacity (reserve GPU pool) or Private (VPC/on-prem) with explicit regional pinning. Dedicated will be the simplest path to meet the P95 250ms objective; Private gives you the tightest walls on data residency.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick call Monday to review the redline and the traffic profile (15–30m).
2) We provide a draft SLA addendum + annotated order form language and an ops runbook showing our monitoring/incident flow.
3) Pilot: we can do a 30-day performance verification pilot under a short T&C with sample metrics collected and a statement of work for ramping to reserved capacity.

I’ve attached a first-pass SLA addendum (redwood-sla-addendum-draft.docx) and our ops runbook (redwood-ops-runbook.pdf) for your legal and cloudops review. A few open items we need from Helix: expected peak qps, typical request size (tokens), and whether you need multi-region active-active or single-region plus failover.

Proposed times for a short call: Mon 11/23 09:30–10:00 PT or 14:00–14:30 PT. Which works?

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales Manager — Redwood Inference

Monica — thanks for the ping and the draft. Technical summary below.

1) Feasibility: On Dedicated capacity (pinned EU region) we can reasonably meet P95 <= 250ms for text-generation endpoints for the traffic profile Helix provided, assuming:
   - Request sizes average <= 200 tokens, burst QPS <= 400, and proper batching settings.
   - Prefix/KV caching is enabled for repeated prompts to reduce latency variability.

2) Measurement: We recommend measuring availability and latency at the API gateway layer per calendar month with the following definitions:
   - Availability: % of successful 2xx responses from generation endpoints excluding scheduled maintenance windows (pre-notified 48h) and force majeure.
   - Latency SLO: P95 of server-side generation time as measured by Redwood's telemetry pipeline (console-traces + edge gateway).

3) Operational controls to include in the addendum:
   - Burst protection: short-term burst capacity (burstable for X hours) and a defined throttling policy.
   - Fallback: automatic fallback to a compatible, lower-cost model variant if Dedicated capacity is exhausted; fallback incurs best-effort SLA (no credit).
   - Evidence package: monthly activity report, raw P95 latency csv samples on request (we can provide a sampling of traces).

4) Suggested order form language snippet (feel free to paste into the draft):

"Service Level: Redwood will maintain 99.95% monthly availability for the Service on Dedicated capacity as defined in this Addendum. Availability and latency will be measured at the API gateway. In the event of a monthly availability breach, Customer may be eligible for service credits as set forth in Section 4. Exclusions include scheduled maintenance (minimum 48-hours notice), Force Majeure, and third-party cloud provider outages.

Pilot clause: Customer may run a 30-day Performance Verification Pilot following execution of this Addendum. During the Pilot Redwood will collect sample telemetry and provide a final performance attestation within 5 business days of Pilot completion."

5) Evidence: attached a small sample export (latency-evidence-samples.csv) showing P50/P95 under similar load for a previous Dedicated deployment.

I’ll be available on the Monday call to talk through knobs (batching, token limits, model variant fallbacks).

— Aditya

Attachments: latency-evidence-samples.csv

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Custom SLA addendum and order form language for Helix Health — legal redlines

Thanks team — quick legal notes / proposed edits to the draft: 

1) Carve-outs: add explicit language for DDoS and Customer misconfiguration; clarify that credits do not apply for breaches due to Customer-supplied third-party integrations.
2) Measurement & Evidence: require Redwood to provide monthly reports and retain telemetry for at least 90 days for audit; preserve Redwood’s right to redact sensitive debug traces.
3) Pilot acceptance: define objective pass criteria (P95 <= 250ms for X out of 4 weeks during pilot, or otherwise a documented remediation plan).
4) Signature path: propose DocuSign flow with two-stage signature (Addendum signed first, Order Form signed on pilot acceptance).

I’ve attached a legal redline with these edits (sla-addendum-legal-redline.docx). Monica—if Helix pushes back on retention of telemetry for 90 days, we can offer a scoped export on request instead of full retention.

-David

Attachments: sla-addendum-legal-redline.docx
